t: You're looking at the Younger Memnon, a colossal granite head and upper torso that came from the Ramesseum, the mortuary temple at Thebes in Upper Egypt. It shows Ramesses II, wearing the Nemes head-dress with a cobra diadem on top. The statue is damaged, and what you see here has been separated from the rest of it, which stays in Egypt. It was one of a pair that flanked the temple's doorway, and the other head still sits at the temple. Ramesses II ruled for sixty-six years, the longest recorded reign of any pharaoh, and is often called the greatest of them.
